compatibility: checkpoint version 2 is required for every new or touched task record; untouched legacy version 1 records remain readable during migration

observation_counter_contract.monotonic_history_rule: a prior exact-SHA entry may never be removed and its ci or review counter may never decrease
observation_counter_contract.migration_rule: every task record touched or created after this policy revision must be checkpoint version 2; untouched version 1 records are legacy-read-only
observation_counter_contract.overflow_rule: observation history is durable and non-evicting; the very large parser bound is defensive input protection, not an archival or eviction threshold

rules: ROTATE is a terminal invocation result and never a checkpoint task status.
Before returning ROTATE, persist ready, waiting or blocked with one concrete next_action.
NOT_APPLICABLE requires a concrete evidence reason.
Checkpoint version 1 is legacy-read-only: every task record changed or created after the version-2 migration policy must use version 2.
Any checkpoint version 2 record must persist CI and review observations in observation_counters_by_sha keyed by exact commit SHA.
For version 2, current-head scalar counters must equal the current head entry in observation_counters_by_sha.
Across a task's Git history, observation entries are append-only by exact SHA and their CI/review counters are monotonic non-decreasing.
Returning from SHA B to previously observed SHA A reuses SHA A counters; owner invocation, Chat replacement, rerun and check-generation changes never reset them.
Prior exact-SHA history must not be evicted; the parser's defensive maximum is intentionally far above any plausible task lifetime and does not authorize deletion.
